3  2025:KER:50813  JUDGMENT Dr. A.K.Jayasankaran Nambiar, J.
This appeal, preferred by the petitioners in W.P.(C) No.23515 of 2021, impugns the judgment dated 24.07.2024 of the learned Single Judge in the writ petition on a very limited point with regard to the permissible use by the appellants of that portion of a building, which was not acquired by the respondents pursuant to the acquisition proceedings initiated by them under the National Highways Act, 1956.

2. The brief facts necessary for the disposal of this writ appeal are as follows:
The appellants are the legal heirs of late P.M. Ibrahim, who was the owner in possession of two shop rooms situated in R.S. No.129/7B in Uppalla Village.

A portion of the land was acquired for the widening of the National Highway, and pursuant to issuance of notices for acquisition, the portion of the land was acquired and an award was passed by the respondents on 11.11.2020.
3.
The grievance of the appellants, as highlighted in their writ petition was with regard to the unacquired portion of the building that continued to remain in their possession and ownership.

It was the case of the appellants that they were being prevented by the respondents from carrying on any activities in the remaining portion of the building that was not acquired, by contending that the National Highways Authority of India ( hereinafter referred to as 'NHAI') had deposited compensation attributable 2025:KER:50813 to the unacquired portion of the building, and therefore they had the right to insist that the appellants not carry on any activities in the said portion of the building.

4. The learned Single Judge who considered the matter found as follows on the said issue at paragraph No.10 of the impugned judgment:
".......10.
Once 3D notification is issued, the land absolutely vests with the Central Government.
Therefore, from that day onwards the petitioners are not the owners of the land acquired.
The petitioners cannot claim that the portion of the building which is not coming in the right of the way be allowed to be retained.

Therefore once the whole building is acquired and Award is passed with respect to the building, the owners of land or the building cannot retain any portion of it, as it has already vested with the Central Government.
Therefore, the prayers sought for in this Petition cannot be allowed and the Writ Petition is dismissed."

5. We have heard Adv. Abdul Raoof Pallipath, the learned counsel for the appellants and Adv. B. G.
Bidan Chandran, the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent NHAI.
We have also heard Asiamma vs *Corrected.

(The Chief Engineer (La) on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57108983/
4 Adv.T.K.Shajahan, the learned Senior Government Pleader for respondents 1 to 3.
6.

On a consideration of the rival submissions, we find that it is an admitted fact that in the notification issued under the National Highways Act for acquisition, the portion of the building that was the 2025:KER:50813 subject matter of the writ petition was not mentioned.

While we are not in a position to ascertain what the amount deposited by the NHAI before the competent authority towards the unacquired portion of the building represents, we are of the view that, so long as the portion of the building remaining in the possession of the appellants was not included in the notification for acquisition under the NHAI Act, the respondents cannot have any right to dictate as to what can be done by the appellants on the said land and the portion of the building situated thereon.

We therefore allow this writ appeal to the limited extent of clarifying that, while the acquired lands with buildings / portions of buildings thereon will vest in the NHAI consequent to the acquisition proceedings initiated under the National Highways Act, they will not have any right whatsoever over the unacquired lands and the portions of the buildings thereon, which continue to be in the possession and ownership of the appellants.
Sd/-
DR. A.K.JAYASANKARAN NAMBIAR JUDGE Sd/-
